text:
Thomas Harley is playing 25:35 a night, and on Nov 15 against Florida he played 30:54 with Dallas down to five defensemen. The Dallas Hoops Journal headline over that one quoted him: "That's My Job." It is now.

He has 15 points in 22 games, ten in his last ten, and Dallas has won four straight. The latest was his goal from distance to tie Thursday's game in Vegas 3-3, a shot Jesse Granger of The Athletic thought slipped through Adin Hill's glove.

Our numbers say this is mostly real. His shooting, 7.3%, sits inside his range, his own chances are steady and the on-ice luck is close to neutral. His scoring pace runs a little ahead of our talent range's middle, but not by much.

The open question is defense. Evolving-Hockey had him around replacement level last season, with opponents getting more expected goals against when he was on. This season Dallas takes 52.8% of expected goals with him on, a bit better than without.

What to watch: Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had 28% of his shots coming off the rush last season, against 17% for a typical defenseman. That's his game when he jumps up.
headline: Harley is carrying Dallas's blue line
